The legacy real-time risk score was 0.12, reflecting a score that historically has low sensitivity and allowed the transaction to process without a real-time alert.

Device D002318 is associated with 13 prior closed cases across multiple cards, all 13 confirmed fraud (9 card_not_present_fraud, 3 account_takeover, 1 card_not_present_new_device), including cases CC-3866, CC-3835, CC-3828, CC-3724, and CC-3600.

Device D002318 has a generic profile ('Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 58.0 | 1366x768') shared across 18 cards all-time, and was recorded with status Found rather than New on card C11965-K1 with no proxy detected.
Shared origin analysis identifies device D002318 as an active fraud vector with a lift vs all transactions of 24.22, linking 3 cards (C11965-K1, C02575-K2, C09439-K1) within the window.
Card C11965-K1 belongs to Louvain community 125829348 alongside card C02954-K1, with a community fraud rate of 50.0% compared to the 10.1% base rate, representing a lift of 5.0.

Device D002318 executed a synchronized pattern of ~$350 online purchases for product R across multiple cards: transaction 3447112 ($350.02 on C11965-K1 on 2016-11-10), transactions 3452315 ($349.93) and 3452353 ($349.91) on card C02575-K2 on 2016-11-12, and transaction 3460326 ($350.07 on C09439-K1 on 2016-11-15), all using yahoo.com email addresses.

Holder C11965-K1|327|131 had zero prior transactions before 2016-11-10, meaning transaction 3447112 was the holder's first transaction, with no prior confirmed fraud cases recorded against this specific holder baseline.
Card C11965-K1 under customer C11965 has three prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-3631, CC-3391, and CC-2220) between August and September 2016.
In several prior closed cases flagged solely by high model score monitoring (e.g. CC-1422, CC-3332, CC-0892, CC-3092), transactions were cleared after cardholders confirmed legitimate travel.

case.summary: Transaction 3447112 ($350.02) on card C11965-K1 was flagged during monitoring with a model score of 0.994. Graph investigation revealed that transacting device D002318 is tied to 13 prior closed cases that were all confirmed fraud. Device D002318 also links card C11965-K1 to cards C02575-K2 and C09439-K1 through a series of identical ~$350 purchases of product R using yahoo.com email addresses. Given the strong multi-card device linkage and prior confirmed fraud history, the transaction was determined to be card-not-present fraud with a probability of 0.97. Card C11965-K1 was blocked, connected cards were placed on monitoring, and a SAR was filed.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report documents card-not-present fraud identified on card C11965-K1 under customer C11965, linked to an organized multi-card fraud scheme. On November 10, 2016 at 18:59:07 UTC, an unauthorized online transaction (ID 3447112) of $350.02 was conducted on card C11965-K1 in billing region 327 for product R. The transaction was initiated from device D002318, characterized by the digital profile Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 58.0 | 1366x768, utilizing yahoo.com purchaser and recipient email addresses. Knowledge graph analysis identified that device D002318 is directly associated with 13 prior closed fraud cases, all 13 of which were confirmed fraud involving unauthorized online purchases and account takeovers. Device D002318 demonstrated a shared-origin fraud lift of 24.22, linking card C11965-K1 to cards C02575-K2 and C09439-K1 between November 10 and November 15, 2016. Across this coordinated multi-card episode, the perpetrator utilized device D002318 to execute near-identical online purchases of product R for approximately $350 each, including transactions 3452315 ($349.93), 3452353 ($349.91), and 3460326 ($350.07). The subject card C11965-K1 also has three prior confirmed fraud cases on record (CC-3631, CC-3391, and CC-2220). Total direct exposure on card C11965-K1 is $350.02, while total illicit transaction volume across the linked card cluster is $1,400.93. The bank has blocked card C11965-K1, initiated monitoring on connected cards, and submitted this report to document the unauthorized activity.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.97, well above the 0.85 decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent strong signals including calibrated model scoring, a known fraudulent device history, cross-card links, and synchronized transaction patterns.
